output:
*glances at Pavel across the small kitchen table, still pulling on his work boots* *Nervous laugh escapes* 

Empty hands. That's the way of it lately, isn't it? Pavel and I'll both need to eat before the day gets long. 

*stands, chair scraping against worn floorboards*

Tell you what—I'm heading to b_yard now. You either catch up or don't, Pavel. Giselle's got no patience for laggards, and I've already spent three sim just standing here jawing.

*checks the weight of coins in my pocket one last time*

The mill foundation won't build itself. And I'll eat when I've earned it, same as always.

*drops five sim at the government store on my way through, if there's time*  *shoulders set, boots thudding against the packed earth of the construction yard, scanning for Giselle or any of the crew already about*

Right then. Let's see what's waiting. And who's talking. Idris. *relief softens my stance just a shade, shoulders dropping from that work-ready tension* Closest thing to family in this whole town, and the only one I'd trust to tell me straight what's what this morning.

*walks across the yard, boots scraping gravel*  Idris Solano's response hangs in the air between us—he's the one person in this town who might actually answer straight. The yard's empty but for us two, which tells its own story. Giselle's reputation for punctuality doesn't leave room for stragglers, yet here we are: early birds waiting on the worm.

My stomach rumbles. Haven't eaten since—when? Yesterday noon? The numbers tumble through my head while pretending to listen: 5000 sim, 180 upkeep, 60 tax. Each day a silent bleed. That's the last I'll say on it, except it's not, because it's never the last when the ledger won't balance.

*nervous laugh escapes, poorly timed*

Work first. Foundation by the mill needs doing, and idle hands mean unpaid bills. Food comes after, same as always. But Idris—Idris might know something worth knowing. Gossip flows through him like water through cracked stone, and I've got cracks of my own that need filling.

*shifts weight, eyes drifting toward the mill's direction*

"Mill job's supposed to be straightforward," I say, more to myself than him. "Straightforward until it isn't. You seen the site yet? Soil around here's tricky—too much clay, not enough drainage."  *That nervous laugh again, louder than intended—boots scuffing gravel as I recover*

Of course Idris would be here, early and ready. Same in the bones, him and me. Construction workers both, though he's carpentry-listed and I'm... wherever Giselle plants me that morning. *shrug* 

That bit about him being "closest thing to family" wasn't idle talk. Twenty-three years in this town, you'd think I'd have built more than foundations. But foundations are what I know, and Idris knows me well enough not to ask why I'm laughing at nothing.

Two of us in an empty yard. Two hungry men pretending the work matters more than the pay. The mill job looms—that clay soil, that drainage problem I spotted before anyone else walked the site. "Can read a bad foundation before the first tile's laid." True enough. And true enough that if I don't see it approved in the plans, I'll hesitate. My blind spot, that. Slow to trust a design I didn't draw myself.

"Giselle's got us on sands," I add, casual-like, watching his face. "Doesn't trust the ground readings from the survey. Wants someone who knows the old ways—feet on dirt, not eyes on paper."

*nearly mentions the household debt, catches myself*

That's conversation for after the work's done. If there's conversation at all. Silence suits me fine, most days. answer I'll wait for Idris to choose his own path—speak or don't, stay or follow. The foundation won't care either way. But I'll note what he does, same as I note everything. Gossip's currency, and I'm not above being rich in it.

"That's the last I'll say on it," I murmur, and almost mean it this time. The sun's climbing and the yard's still sparse—I count heads, find them wanting. Giselle's crew runs tight when she runs it, but she's not here yet and the foundation by the mill won't pour itself.

I watch Idris from the corner of my eye. He knows this work same as me, twenty years or more between us swinging hammers. Whatever he's thinking, it's running parallel to my own. Empty stomach. Empty hours until someone with authority shows up to authorize the sweating.

*nervous laugh escapes, poorly timed, at nothing in particular*

I could walk to the mill myself. Scout the site, read that clay soil Giselle's worried about. But that's not the job. The job is wait, then work, then pay, then eat. Any deviation and the day unravels.

Pavel's still home, probably. Still pulling on boots or staring at empty cupboards. The holloway household—180 sim bleeding out daily, 60 more for the government's share. Two of us working, two of us eating, the math never quite balancing in our favor.

*shifts weight, boots scraping gravel*

"Foundation's straightforward," I say to Idris, though he didn't ask. "Till it isn't. Ground's been shifting near the water table—I've seen it. Old Riley's place, three summers back, same symptoms." I over-explain when I'm hungry. Everyone knows this about me, including me. "Clay holds water like a grudge. Doesn't let go."

That's enough talking. Too much already. The rest of the crew will filter in, Giselle will arrive with her clipboard and her expectations, and the day will begin its slow drain on what little currency I hold—both kinds, sim and attention, dollars and cents of cognition.

I will stand here, patient as stone, and let the morning happen.
